legal.attributions_intro: VIRE is built on open data and third-party services. Here are the sources used in the app, their licenses and links to their producers.
legal.src_osm: Places and trails database, and route computation (self-hosted GraphHopper engine on OpenStreetMap data).
legal.src_datatourisme: Tourist points of interest in France, published by tourist offices through the national DATAtourisme platform (Direction générale des Entreprises).
legal.src_wikidata: Listed villages (Les Plus Beaux Villages de France, I borghi più belli d'Italia) and place notability scores.
legal.src_geotrek: Hiking routes published by parks: PNR des Ballons des Vosges, Écrins National Park and Vanoise National Park (Geotrek portals).
legal.src_copernicus: Elevations and elevation-gain computation (Copernicus DEM GLO-30 terrain model, served by a self-hosted OpenTopoData instance).
legal.src_photos: Trip illustration photos, used in accordance with the Unsplash and Pexels licenses.
legal.src_ademe: Fuel CO₂e emission factors (ADEME Base Carbone®, well-to-wheel) used for the carbon-footprint estimate.
legal.src_mapbox: Base maps and interactive map rendering.
legal.tdm_intro: VIRE enriches its places database by automatically extracting geographic facts from public outdoor web content. This notice summarises what we collect, on what legal basis, and how to opt out.
legal.french_prevails: This notice is legally binding in French only — the French version prevails.
legal.tdm_what_body: Only facts about places: name, type, coordinates and short tags. Never article text, never photos, never information about authors or other people. Any personal data detected is rejected before storage, and every fact is cross-checked against open sources (OpenStreetMap, DATAtourisme, Wikidata).
legal.tdm_why_body: To improve the relevance of the outdoor itineraries offered to VIRE users, by grounding suggestions on real, verified places. No purpose involves profiling people.
legal.tdm_legal_body: Intellectual property: the text and data mining exception (Article 4 of Directive (EU) 2019/790; Article L.122-5-3 of the French Intellectual Property Code), with opt-outs systematically honoured. Personal data: legitimate interest, with strict safeguards (minimisation, rejection filters, audit log); hosting within the European Union, no transfers outside the EU.
legal.tdm_optout_body: Before any access, we check and honour robots.txt (RFC 9309), ai.txt, the noai / notdm meta tags, the TDMRep protocol and opt-out statements expressed in natural language. The opt-out status is re-checked on every access and recorded in our source register (tdm_sources). Our crawler identifies itself with the user agent “VIRE-TDM”, with an information URL and a contact address.
legal.tdm_rights_body: Website publishers and data subjects: you can request the exclusion of a site or the erasure of facts derived from a source. Erasure is carried out by deleting the records concerned and adding the site to our permanent exclusion list.
legal.src_commons: Geolocated photos of trip places (coordinate search), shown in the map carousel with author and licence.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what data VIRE collects, why, and what your rights are. In short: we collect only what is strictly necessary to run the service, we sell no data, and we use no advertising cookies.
privacy.data_body:
When you create an account, we collect your email address and a password (stored in hashed form, never in plain text). Authentication is handled by Supabase, hosted in the AWS eu-central-1 region (Frankfurt, Germany).

The itineraries you create (trips, stages, preferences) are stored on our server located in the European Union. Your browser also keeps a few technical items locally (chosen language, session).
privacy.purpose_body:
Your data is used solely to provide the service: creating your account, saving your itineraries and running the application. The legal basis is the performance of the service you requested, together with our legitimate interest in keeping the site secure and working properly.

We do no commercial prospecting, no advertising profiling, and we pass no data to third parties for advertising purposes.
privacy.processors_body:
To operate, VIRE relies on a few service providers: Supabase (authentication), Mapbox (map display — your browser sends it tile requests that include your IP address), Unsplash, Pexels and Wikimedia Commons (photos), Deepseek and Anthropic (AI itinerary generation) and Open-Meteo (weather).

The messages you send in the chat are transmitted to Deepseek or Anthropic to generate your itineraries, without any personal identifier: neither your email, nor your name, nor your IP address is shared with them.

PostHog EU (anonymous audience measurement, data hosted in the EU).
privacy.rights_body:
Under the GDPR, you can at any time access your data, have it corrected or deleted, and object to or request the restriction of its processing. Simply write to jules.million07@gmail.com; we reply within one month at most.

If you believe your rights are not being respected, you can lodge a complaint with the French data protection authority, the CNIL (cnil.fr).
privacy.cookies_body:
VIRE uses no advertising cookies and no third-party trackers. Only your browser's local storage (localStorage) is used, for strictly technical needs: remembering your language and keeping your session active.

Since this storage is essential to the operation of the service, no cookie consent banner is required — which is why you do not see one.

Audience measurement: VIRE uses PostHog (hosted in the European Union) in a strictly anonymous, cookie-free mode — no identifier is written to your device, visits are never linked together, and the content of your requests is never transmitted. Your browser's "Do Not Track" signal is honoured; you can also disable this measurement from the browser console with: localStorage.setItem('triptic-analytics', 'off').
privacy.retention_body:
Your account data and itineraries are kept for as long as your account is active. If you delete your account or request its deletion by email, all of your data is erased.

Itineraries you choose to make public remain visible until you unpublish or delete them. The server's technical logs are kept for a short period, for security and debugging purposes only.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Welcome to VIRE. By using the service, you accept these terms. VIRE is currently offered free of charge: no payment is collected.
terms.service_body:
VIRE is a web application for planning outdoor adventures (road trips, treks, bikepacking). It generates itinerary suggestions using artificial intelligence, which you can then edit, save and share.

The service is provided as is, with no guarantee of continuous availability. Paid plans may be offered in the future; they will then be covered by specific terms.
terms.account_body:
Creating an account is required to save your itineraries. You agree to provide a valid email address and to keep your password confidential.

You can delete your account at any time; your data will then be erased in accordance with the privacy policy.
terms.content_body:
You remain the owner of the itineraries you create. Sharing an itinerary publicly is your voluntary choice: anyone with the link will then be able to view it.

You agree not to publish content that is unlawful, misleading or infringes the rights of others. We may remove any content that breaches these terms.
terms.liability_body:
The itineraries suggested by VIRE are provided for guidance only. They may contain errors or inaccuracies, in particular because they are partly generated by artificial intelligence.

Before setting off, always check local conditions, the weather, the state of trails and roads, and the applicable regulations (protected areas, wild camping, traffic rules). Outdoor activities involve risks: you undertake them at your own responsibility, and the publisher cannot be held liable for accidents or incidents occurring during your trips.
terms.changes_body:
These terms may change, in particular when new features or paid plans are introduced. In the event of a significant change, you will be informed through the application.

Continuing to use the service after a change constitutes acceptance of the new terms.
